find: EU sugar subsidies, for example, made it cheaper for African producers to sell cane sugar to Europe than for Europeans to buy it — until the subsidies were reformed.
replace: EU sugar subsidies, for example, kept European beet sugar artificially cheap, so African cane growers struggled to compete — until the system was reformed.
note: F7: the original sentence is garbled and states the effect of subsidies backwards.

find: HS2, the proposed high-speed line from London to Birmingham (and originally to Manchester and Leeds), is the highest-profile example. Northern Powerhouse Rail and Crossrail upgrades aim to do the same.
